title: interactive-playback-cli-with-telemetry-sanitizer-and-noise-filter
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: Oncall runs frequently need to reproduce incidents locally for debugging. Replay tooling exists but is either heavyweight or leaks sensitive PII/keys. This PR adds an interactive CLI playback tool wired into incident-bot that performs deterministic event/time replay with a configurable telemetry sanitizer and noise-suppression heuristics. Features: 1) CLI 'rb-play' command to load a sanitized incident bundle and step/seek through spans, logs and metrics; 2) deterministic time-scaling and step-forward/back controls to reproduce race conditions; 3) pluggable sanitizer pipeline: redaction rules (regex), token masking, host and IP obfuscation, and KMS-backed secret revocation markers; 4) automatic noise filter that collapses repetitive noisy alerts (rate-limited grouping) and suggests silence rules based on signal-to-noise heuristics; 5) exportable ephemeral runbook draft that captures the exact playback steps and context for postmortem; 6) lightweight web preview server for team members to view sanitized playback without granting storage access. Implementation notes: the tool is implemented in Go inside cmd/rb-play, with sanitizer rules under incident-bot/sanitizers, and a small playback harness in internal/playback that replays events against the same instrumentation adapters used in prod. Backwards compatibility: the bundle format is a superset of the existing incident snapshot format; older bundles still load but will skip sanitizer annotations. Testing: unit tests added for sanitizer rules, integration tests for playback determinism (CI harness uses a golden trace), and an optional e2e job that runs the web preview against a small sample bundle (flaky, gated). Checklist: - [x] CLI implementation and docs - [x] Sanitizer rule engine with tests - [x] Noise suppression heuristics - [x] Integration tests for determinism - [x] Documentation and quickstart - [x] UX review and demo to SRE. Related: Linear ENG-2214 (playback UX), ENG-2330 (sanitizer rule set), Jira SUP-4121 (support ticket requesting local repro).

review_comments: Ethan Clarke: Nice surface. Can we avoid pulling the prod KMS key into the dev workflow? Suggest adding a KMS-mock mode and documenting keyless dev path.
Maya Chen: Good point — added KMS-mock and documented it in docs/playback-quickstart.md. The sanitizer will emit revocation markers instead of encrypted tokens when mock mode is enabled.
Ravi Patel: Integration test timing is flaky on CI; the golden trace sometimes diverges on scheduling. Can we make the harness tolerate minor timestamp jitter?
Maya Chen: Updated integration harness to normalize timestamps to ms and added retry/backoff. CI job moved to optional-e2e group to avoid blocking merges.
Laura Gómez: UX: the web preview should hide internal hostnames by default. I see the sanitizer covers this; confirm default policy is 'hide'.
Maya Chen: Confirmed — default policy is 'hide', added a note in docs and the CLI prints the active sanitizer profile when running.
Ethan Clarke: Lint failed initially; I responded with fixes in f2b7d11 and CI now passes. Approving after CI green.
Ravi Patel: Approved. Good to merge once e2e flakiness is tracked (ENG-2330).
